text:
Elena (People Ops): quick one 1 1 we had a vendor dinner in Amsterdam last night. I paid the full bill on my personal card for the whole table and want to submit for reimbursement split across four employees. What's the preferred process for itemizing split dinners and tip policy?

Marco G: thanks. was this a client dinner or internal team-only? tip amount?

Elena (People Ops): internal team-only, 4 people. bill = 198.50 EUR including service. I left the detailed itemized receipt but the restaurant printed one total line + service. I can attach the merchant receipt and my personal card statement showing the charge.

Priya S: for internal meals we reimburse per-person share. since you covered the whole bill, submit as one expense with the attendees listed and then include per-person amounts in the notes. Finance prefers an explicit split so they can code to different cost centers if needed.

Finance Bot: Automated guideline: 
```
- Attach original itemized receipt or merchant receipt (photo OK)
- Upload proof of payment (personal-card statement screenshot last 4 digits)
- In the "Notes" field list attendees and their email + share amount (e.g., Marco G (marco@) - 49.63)
- If attendees are charged to different cost centers, include charge codes per person
- For tips/service included: indicate whether tip is optional or mandatory service charge
- Select expense category: "Meals - Team/Internal"
```

Tom L: is the service line considered "tip"? in NL it's usually a small service charge but restaurants vary. do we reimburse service charges?

Rachel (Legal): policy: we reimburse reasonable tips/service up to 20% for international travel, but if the service charge is VAT-able and reclaimable we treat it as part of the invoice. Finance will handle VAT recovery if the receipt has VAT. If no VAT breakdown, we still reimburse but can't reclaim VAT.

Priya S: also note per-diem rules: if travelers are on per-diem for the trip, you can't double-claim actual meal expenses. This was not on per-diem.

Elena (People Ops): great. what about rounding / cents? dividing 198.50 by 4 is 49.625. do we round per person or give one person the extra cent?

Finance Bot: rounding guidance: allocate to cents (two decimals). Example: two people 49.63, two people 49.62. Put the full math in the notes. Finance prefers explicit per-person amounts; they will reimburse exact listed amounts.

Marco G: i'll pay my share back to Elena personally via bank transfer if that's faster, so she can submit our receipts as "internal reimbursement - group" with a note saying Marco reimbursed Elena 49.63 on 2026-06-01. is that allowed?

Finance Bot: Personal reimbursements between employees are allowed but discouraged. If you reimburse Elena, she must attach proof of that transfer (screenshot or bank confirmation) and then record the attendee list to show no duplicate claims. Finance will accept either direct reimburse or individual expense submissions; whichever gets receipts attached and avoids duplicated claims is fine.

Elena (People Ops): final check 1 do I mark expense as "Out-of-pocket (urgent)" so each person can get quicker small refunds?

Finance Bot: For small internal splits, choose standard submission. If any person needs urgent reimbursement, that individual should submit their own claim or use the "urgent" flag; avoid splitting urgent vs non-urgent on the same ticket.

Priya S: thanks everyone. i'll paste this checklist to the group and include the exact split amounts.

Elena (People Ops): thanks all :raised_hands: everyone except Marco is on company card next time :grin:
